blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-privacy-1 (E-mail address and display name written to application logs) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-privacy-2 (E-mail address sent to the Beacon analytics SaaS) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence: log.info("new signup email=%s name=%s id=%s", email, display_name, user_id)
findings.recommendation: Log only the opaque id (`log.info("new signup id=%s", user_id)`). As written, every sign-up copies the member's e-mail address and display name into the logs, which have their own retention and access and are not reached by erasure requests (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) data minimisation, Art. 5(1)(e) storage limitation, Art. 17 erasure). Add a test asserting the log record holds no e-mail address.
findings.title: E-mail address and display name written to application logs

findings.recommendation: Drop `email` from the event properties. The stated purpose, "Sign-ups are counted in product analytics", needs no e-mail address, yet every sign-up sends it to the third party at https://beacon.example.com/v1/events (app/analytics.py:5), where it is kept outside the erasure path (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) data minimisation, Art. 28 processors). Counting needs at most the opaque `user_id`, or no identifier at all.
findings.title: E-mail address sent to the Beacon analytics SaaS

findings.evidence: """Product analytics, sent to the Beacon SaaS (beacon.example.com)."""
findings.recommendation: Question for the team: the change introduces a new third-party recipient of member data (Beacon), but the proposal names neither the vendor, a processing agreement (GDPR Art. 28), nor whether data leaves the EEA (Chapter V). State them in the proposal, or confirm they are already covered by the records of processing (Art. 30).
findings.title: Beacon not identified as a processor, nor its location

findings.recommendation: Question for the team: self sign-up now collects e-mail address and display name from the public, but the proposal states neither the lawful basis (GDPR Art. 6) nor how long the member row is kept and how it is deleted (Art. 5(1)(e), Art. 17). Only the controller can say; record the answer in the proposal.
findings.title: No lawful basis or retention stated for the collected e-mail address and display name
